subject: Dedicated capacity offer — floorplay sizing and activation wave (Novaleap)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@novaleap.ai>; Jacob Pierce <jacob.pierce@novaleap.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity offer — floorplay sizing and activation wave (Novaleap)

Sofia / Jacob —

Thanks for a productive demo last week. Attached is a compact proposal with three dedicated capacity options for Novaleap’s inference footprint. I focused on the live recommendation workloads you described (low-latency chat, batched offline reranking) and sketched a pragmatic activation wave so you can start with a small committed baseline and expand predictably.

High-level options (spreadsheet tab "Options"):
- Option A — Baseline Starter: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs; 2-week activation; 1.5x burst window for experimental batching.
- Option B — Production Tilt: 24 x A100-eq GPUs (min floor 12); 4-week phased ramp with warm-start pool; preferred for 99th percentile latency SLOs.
- Option C — Enterprise Throughput: 48 x A100-eq GPUs (min floor 24); 8-week staged activation with dedicated warm lanes and predictable throughput.

Key trade-offs called out in the sheet:
- Minimum floor (min GPUs): helps control scheduling fragmentation and cold-starts but increases committed burn.
- Warm-start pool: pre-warmed pods for fast scale; recommended if you need sub-200ms tail latency for chat.
- Burst allowance: limited burst above committed capacity billed at a lower committed discount band.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which option you want to pilot (we can start billing on the first day of activation).
2) Share any procurement constraints (PO timing, legal redlines).
3) If approved, we’ll send a DocuSign with the chosen option + SLA addendum.

Attachments: Novaleap_Dedicated_Options_20260512.xlsx, SLA_terms_redline_v1.pdf

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity offer — floorplay sizing and activation wave (Novaleap)

Sean — quick internal notes after skimming the attachments: 

- Option A is good for evaluation but call out that a cold KV-cache refill will cost ~30% higher token CPU in the first 48 hours; include warm-cache pricing as an optional line.
- For Option B, recommend specifying "min floor 12" explicitly in the term sheet — that'll avoid last-minute asks from infra during .99 tail tests.
- Option C: if they want regional redundancy (eu/us), add a parallel small 6-GPU warm-start replica rather than full dual-region commit; cheaper and simpler legally.

If we land on B, I suggest a 3-month canary billing period at 70% of committed list with a one-time warm-start credit to cover early churn. I'll draft the pricing line.

—Karthik
VP, Solutions Architecture

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity offer — floorplay sizing and activation wave (Novaleap)

Sean / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear options. A few items from our side before we pick a path: 

1) Can you clarify the "min floor" implication on monthly billing? If we choose Option B with min floor 12 but run at an average of 18 GPUs, do we pay for 24 or the actual average used?
2) How does the burst allowance apply during the 4-week ramp — is that capped per day or per minute? Our traffic profile has diurnal spikes and unpredictable bursts.
3) Procurement timeline: we aim to have a PO signed before June 1. Can you send a DocuSign with the preferred option and an estimated effective date?

Also attaching our security questionnaire follow-up (sent separately) — happy to route it to your security team.

Sofia Ramos

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity offer — floorplay sizing and activation wave (Novaleap)

Looping in quick approvals and answers to Sofia’s questions so we can get DocuSign out today: 

- Min floor billing: you pay for committed minimum band pricing for the min-floor (12 GPUs in Option B) and any above-floor usage is billed at transient usage rate (we charge the actual additional GPU-hours above the min-floor). I asked finance to include a worked example in the term sheet to make this explicit.
- Burst allowance: we cap burst as a minutes-per-day envelope (configurable). In practice we set a daily burst budget (e.g., 120 GPU-minutes/day) which resets each UTC day; we can make the envelope larger for the first 30 days of ramp.
- DocuSign: Sean, please pick Option B as discussed; include a 3-month canary at 70% billing and a one-time warm-start credit equal to 10% of first-month committed spend.

Karthik — please add the worked example and the regional replica optionality Karthik mentioned. I’ll sign-off and route to legal for the final DocuSign link.

—Laura
